prompt.context: Your client, Specialty Pharma, is a specialty pharmaceutical company looking to grow its revenue. They are similar to a pharmacy within a CVS; however, they are attached to community mental health facilities.
prompt.question: What are some ways your client can grow revenues?

clarifying_info.q: Is the client focused on revenue only, or also on profitability?
clarifying_info.a: At this point, Specialty Pharma is only interested in growing revenue, without taking costs into account.

clarifying_info.q: Does Specialty Pharma currently operate pharmacies outside of community health centers?
clarifying_info.a: Currently Specialty Pharma only operates pharmacies within community health centers; they have not tried to open pharmacies outside of community health facilities.

exhibits.title: Community Mental Health Centers and Pharmacy Ownership
exhibits.shows: A breakdown of the ~4,000 community mental health centers in the US, showing how many have an attached pharmacy, and the ownership split of those pharmacies between the Community Mental Health Center, third-party vendors, and Specialty Pharma.

framework: Internal Growth: Offer new drug forms / expand beyond mental-health drugs; offer new services (delivery, passport photos, etc.); increase number of patients per pharmacy via local marketing; increase prescription adherence; offer loyalty programs

External Growth: Find new community health facilities in which to open pharmacies; explore opening pharmacies outside mental-health facilities; partner with drug companies for discounts to increase sales
Note: the question is about revenue only — costs may be mentioned but are not the focus

questions.prompt: Q1 – Market Sizing: What would you estimate the market size for Specialty Pharma to be?
questions.guidance: Classic market sizing. Candidate may scope to mental-health-related drugs or size the general pharmacy market. Key is a structured, reasonable chain of assumptions. After the general sizing, show Exhibit 1 and ask: How many stores does Specialty Pharma currently have?

math.setup: Size the US mental-health pharmacy market; then use Exhibit 1 to back into current store count.
steps: ~1 in 5 Americans has mental-health issues (20%) → 64M potential customers
~50% seek treatment; of those, 80% go to community mental health facilities (20% go to hospitals) → 64M × 50% × 80% = 25.6M patients
Assume all patients at community health facilities buy drugs on-site → market = ~25.6M patients
Exhibit 1 store count: 440 total attached pharmacies; 60% third-party; 70% of those owned by Specialty Pharma → 440 × 0.6 × 0.7 = 184.8 ≈ 176 stores (casebook rounds to 176)
math.answer: Market size ~$51.2B; Specialty Pharma currently owns approximately 176 stores

questions.prompt: Q2 – Brainstorming: What additional factors would you consider when thinking about how many additional stores Specialty Pharma could open?
questions.guidance: Brainstorming question — structure and relevance matter most. Strong answers are organized into buckets.

questions.prompt: Q3 – Break-even math: Fixed cost per pharmacy is $250K/year and marginal revenue per prescription is $25. How many prescriptions per day would need to be filled to break even for each new pharmacy?
questions.guidance: Simple mental math. Variable costs can be disregarded if asked. Candidate should state their working-days assumption clearly and comment on whether the resulting number is high or low relative to expectations.

math.setup: Break-even daily prescriptions = (Annual fixed cost / working days) / revenue per prescription
steps: Working days: ~260 (or 360 if open every day — push toward 260 to simplify)
math.answer: 40 prescriptions per day per new pharmacy to break even — a relatively low number, suggesting expansion is not very risky

questions.prompt: Q4 – White space: What is the white space opportunity for expansion? (Assume 30% of all community health centers are large enough to fit a pharmacy.)
questions.guidance: Use Exhibit 1. Candidate must subtract existing pharmacies from the addressable set and comment on whether the number represents a meaningful opportunity.

math.setup: White space = (large-enough health centers) − (existing pharmacies with any owner)
math.answer: 760 additional locations available — a large opportunity relative to the 440 that currently exist, nearly 2× the current footprint

questions.prompt: Q5a – Brainstorming: What concerns would you have about management in this expansion?
questions.guidance: Structured brainstorming relevant to the specifics of this case. Strong answers separate internal from external concerns.

questions.prompt: Q5b – Recommendation: You run into the CEO. What do you tell him about your analysis?
questions.guidance: Quick, crisp synthesis: state the opportunity, whether to pursue it, how, the risks, and next steps. Should mirror the conclusion slide structure.

brainstorming.prompt: What additional factors would you consider when thinking about how many additional stores Specialty Pharma could open? AND What concerns would you have about management in this expansion?

categories.name: Market (expansion factors)
ideas: Size and volume of drugs dispensed each year
Trends and changes in the drugs market

categories.name: Competitive Landscape (expansion factors)
ideas: How will competitors react to expansion?
Where does Specialty Pharma have a competitive edge?

categories.name: Location (expansion factors)
ideas: Proximity to Specialty Pharma's own existing stores (cannibalization risk)

categories.name: External Concerns (management)
ideas: Relationships / agreements with mental health facilities

recommendation: Specialty Pharma should expand and open new pharmacies to grow revenue
There is a large white space of ~760 additional locations in community mental health centers
The break-even threshold of 40 prescriptions per day is low, making the financial risk of each new pharmacy manageable
risks: Competitor reaction from existing pharmacy operators
Management capacity and expertise to handle rapid expansion
Potential changes in the drug market or government reimbursement
next_steps: Begin locating and evaluating community mental health facilities large enough to accommodate a pharmacy
Assess management team's readiness and identify any capability gaps
Develop a phased expansion plan prioritizing highest-potential locations
